chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Faḍālah, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Ḥakam ibn Ḥukaym, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام about ghusl (ritual bath) for janābah, and he said:

“Pour water onto your right palm and wash it, then wash whatever impurity has affected your body, then wash your private part, and pour water over your head and body, then perform ghusl. If you are in a clean place, it does not harm you not to wash your feet; but if you are in a place that is not clean, then wash your feet.”
I said: The people say that one performs wudu (ablution) like the wudu of salat (prayer) before ghusl. So he laughed and said: “What wudu is purer and more far-reaching than ghusl?”

key_terms.أَذًى: impurity or harmful filth affecting the body
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath required due to janābah

ai.seo_question: How should ghusl for janābah be performed, and is wudu needed before it?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the method of ghusl for janābah, beginning with washing the hand, removing filth from the body, washing the private part, and then pouring water over the head and body. It also indicates that washing the feet depends on the cleanliness of the place, and that ghusl itself suffices without needing a separate wudu beforehand.
